summary: trust-escrow is a documentation-only ClawHub skill (no executable scripts) that teaches an agent to create and manage USDC escrows for agent-to-agent payments on Base Sepolia, with single and batch create/release/cancel/dispute/autoRelease calls. To use it the operator/agent must supply a wallet private key (signing key), the escrow contract address 0x6354869F9B79B2Ca0820E171dc489217fC22AD64, the Base Sepolia USDC token 0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e, and the RPC host https://sepolia.base.org plus the trust-escrow-web.vercel.app platform/docs endpoints. The declared metadata requires nothing (no env vars, no binaries), yet the instructions embed a private key and links to remote hosts that are not declared.

findings.message: The workflow example calls privateKeyToAccount('0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY'), instructing the operator to supply a raw wallet private key for signing transactions in plaintext.
The risks section states the skill's examples can sign blockchain transactions, i.e. they drive a wallet credential/private key for escrow actions.
The example imports privateKeyToAccount from viem/accounts and uses a signing key, but the release's metadata requires.env declares nothing.
The skill depends on the Base Sepolia RPC https://sepolia.base.org, a host/endpoint not declared in metadata requires.
createWalletClient uses transport: http() against the Base Sepolia RPC at https://sepolia.base.org to broadcast transactions.
The skill points the agent at https://trust-escrow-web.vercel.app/llms.txt and other vercel.app endpoints (agent-info, skill.md) as remote resources to fetch.
Front-matter metadata declares only requires.network base-sepolia, so its stated requirements disagree with the private key and hosts the instructions actually use.
Mitigation advises verifying network, address, amount, decimals, deadline and allowance size and requiring explicit human review before wallet signing.
